title: Who do you admire?
subtitle: A few minutes. No right answers.

steps.body:
The qualities you most admire in others often belong to you — undeveloped, unexpressed, but present.

The ache you feel when you witness someone living a quality freely — that ache is the shadow's way of pointing home.

steps.title: Who comes to mind?
steps.body: Someone you genuinely admire — a person you know, a public figure, a character. Just one name.

steps.title: What specific quality do they have that moves you?
steps.body: Not 'they're great.' Something precise — 'she says hard things with warmth,' 'he creates without needing approval.'

steps.title: How much does {quality|this quality} move you?
steps.body: The strength of the pull is the signal.
That landed with some weight. Take one breath here before going on — there's no rush.

steps.title: If {quality|that quality} already existed in you — even as a seed — where would you see it?
steps.body: Even if it's tiny, inconsistent, or only in private.

steps.title: What's kept {quality|this quality} from growing in you?
steps.body: What was the early message about it?

exit.body: Whatever you can perceive in others, you have some capacity to perceive it with. The recognition you felt — that's already yours.
